newsitem.title: UK: Bass seen needing to make concessions for takeover.
newsitem.headline: Bass seen needing to make concessions for takeover.

text.p: Bass Plc may have to make big concessions to get regulators' approval for its planned acquisition of Carlsberg-Tetley, rival brewers and pub owners said in interviews with the Financial Times.
The Office of Fair Trading (OFT) is investigating the planned merger and has sent questionnaires to brewers and pub owners asking what they think will happen to prices.
The Financial Times said Bass may be forced to sell pubs, breweries or labels to satisfy the OFT.
"Bass will have to give up a lot more of its pub estate than people think," it quoted a brewery chief executive as saying.
The chief executive of an unnamed competing brewer told the paper that beer prices could rise if Bass increases its market share to between 35 and 38 percent from 23 percent.
"The domination of Bass with all its pubs, its heavy investment in them and its breweries has to make the rest of the industry uncomfortable," the head of anther pub chain agreed.
Bass has said that independent pub chains are driving such hard bargains with brewers that little will change after the merger.
